credential: API Central project client credentials (client ID/secret + mutual TLS certificate)
steps: Reset project credentials in API Central; replace the certificate; remove portal members.
notes: Tokens last up to 60 minutes.

credential: Marketplace data connector client credentials (held by partner app)
steps: Deny the app in Consent Manager and cancel the Marketplace subscription.
notes: ADP validates consent before processing API calls, so denial should block calls; immediate effect on live tokens not stated.

credential: Marketplace Partner API / Data Connector credentials (partner-level)
steps: Customer: deny consent / cancel subscription. Partner: reset credentials in Self Service portal.
notes: Client side: revoking consent in Consent Manager turns the integration off instantly. Partner credential reset timing not documented.

steps: Disable (reversible) or delete (archive) the key; or remove the user from the org.
notes: Docs say the key stops working but give no timing.

steps: Disable/delete the key or archive the service account.
Disable/delete the key or archive its workspace.
notes: Workspace archive archives keys within seconds.

steps: Deactivate or delete the admin key in Console > Settings > Admin keys.
notes: Deleting an Admin API key takes effect on the next request, with no grace period.

steps: Archive the federation rule (then issuer/service account).
notes: Archiving a federation rule stops new exchanges immediately, but tokens already minted stay valid until they expire (default 3600s, max 86400s).

credential: OAuth bearer token (ant CLI login, incl. org:admin)
steps: Remove the user's admin role or remove the user; locally run ant auth logout.
notes: No admin revocation of CLI tokens documented.

steps: Admin: Insights > API token activity > Revoke (or DELETE /v1/orgs/{orgId}/api-tokens for all managed user tokens); owner: id.atlassian.com > Revoke / Revoke all. Optionally block user API token access via authentication policy; deactivate account.
notes: Token is sent on each request (Basic/Bearer), so revocation stops further calls; propagation delay not documented for user tokens (service-account tokens: up to 10 min). Revocation is permanent.

steps: User revokes the grant on their Connected apps screen; admin uninstalls the 3LO app (revokes all users) and can enable 'Block user apps'; reset password / deactivate the user.
notes: Docs say access tokens work until expiry or revocation and the app cannot work after the user revokes consent. Only the user can revoke a single grant; admins can only uninstall the app. No timing stated.

steps: Admin > Directory > Service accounts > Credentials > Revoke (or Revoke credentials for all); API DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/oauth-clients/{clientId}; delete the service account.
notes: Revocation removes the credential; docs don't say if already-issued access tokens (valid 60 min) are invalidated, so assume up to 60 minutes of residual access.

steps: Admin > Directory > Service accounts > select account > Credentials > Revoke; or DELETE /v1/orgs/{orgId}/service-accounts/{serviceAccountId}/api-tokens to revoke all; delete the service account.
notes: Revocation can take up to 10 minutes to take effect. Permanent; reissue a new token.

steps: UpdateAccessKey Status=Inactive, then DeleteAccessKey. Also attach aws:TokenIssueTime deny to the user to block STS sessions the key may have minted.
notes: Deactivation stops the key immediately, but temporary credentials already obtained with it (GetSessionToken/AssumeRole) stay valid until expiry unless permissions are also changed.

steps: Delete the key as root, or from the management account via centralized root access management.
notes: Root permissions cannot be scoped down by IAM policy, so deletion is the only fix.

credential: IAM role temporary credentials (AWS STS AssumeRole)
steps: IAM > Roles > Revoke active sessions (AWSRevokeOlderSessions) or deny aws:TokenIssueTime before now; fix trust policy.
notes: Applies to all sessions of the role, not just one; ~30 s propagation; not possible for service-linked roles.

credential: OIDC / SAML federation to IAM roles (AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, AssumeRoleWithSAML)
steps: Revoke active sessions on the role; tighten trust policy conditions (aud/sub); remove or disable at the IdP.
notes: Role-wide revocation.

credential: IAM Identity Center credentials for AWS CLI/SDK
steps: Add user ID to pre-staged SCP deny, remove assignments, disable user.
notes: Disabling the user alone leaves existing role sessions working up to 12 h.

credential: IAM Roles Anywhere (X.509 certificate to role session)
steps: Import CRL listing the certificate; revoke active sessions on the role; disable trust anchor/profile.
notes: CRL blocks new sessions; existing sessions need role session revocation.

steps: Deactivate, reset or delete the key; or deny bedrock:CallWithBearerToken.
notes: Docs do not state propagation timing.

steps: Invalidate the generating session (revoke role sessions) or deny bedrock:CallWithBearerToken.
notes: Short-term keys expire with the session (max 12 h).

steps: Regenerate the exposed key (and the other if unsure); or set AllowSharedKeyAccess=false.
notes: Regenerating also revokes SAS signed with that key; dependent apps break.

credential: Shared access signatures (SAS): account SAS, service SAS, user delegation SAS
steps: Account/service SAS: regenerate signing key or change stored access policy. User delegation SAS: revoke-delegation-keys. Or disallow Shared Key.
notes: User delegation revocation may be delayed by caching.

credential: Service principal client secrets and certificates (used against Azure Resource Manager)
steps: Remove the secret/certificate, disable the SP, and remove role assignments.
notes: ARM access tokens remain valid until expiry (60-90 min); CAE for workload identities covers Microsoft Graph only.

steps: Delete the federated identity credential; remove role assignments.
notes: Issued access tokens last 60-90 min.

steps: Owner revokes in user settings; admins revoke via Token Admin API or disable the user.
notes: Up to 1 h delay for admin revocation; established connections may persist.

credential: API tokens (Atlassian account API tokens with Bitbucket scopes)
steps: Revoke in API token activity (org admin) or Atlassian account > Security (user); also deactivate the account if compromised.
notes: Revoked tokens no longer work.

steps: None needed; Bitbucket rejects app passwords since 2026-07-28.
notes: Platform-wide removal.

steps: Revoke on the container's Access tokens page.
notes: Content the token created remains.

steps: Delete the consumer in Workspace settings > OAuth consumers (kills all its tokens); or rotate secret.
notes: Deletion removes all existing tokens linked to the consumer.

credential: SSH keys (personal SSH keys and repository/project access keys)
steps: Delete key via UI or DELETE API.
notes: In-flight SSH sessions not documented.

steps: Tighten or delete the trust policy at the resource server; set oidc false.
notes: Already-issued cloud credentials last until their own expiry.

steps: POST /oauth2/revoke with client_id, client_secret and the access or refresh token; admin can disable the user-auth app in Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps.
notes: Revoke acts on the presented token; whether other tokens the same user granted the app are killed, and whether disabling the app ends live tokens, is not documented.

steps: Rotate/revoke the client secret in Developer Console > Configuration; revoke live tokens via POST /oauth2/revoke; admin disables or deauthorizes the server app in Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps.
notes: Revoking one access token does not stop minting new ones while the secret is valid; effect of secret rotation on already-issued 60-min tokens is not documented.

steps: Delete the compromised public key in Developer Console (Add and Manage Public Keys) and rotate client secret; revoke live tokens via POST /oauth2/revoke; admin disables/deauthorizes the server app in Admin Console.
notes: Max two keypairs; check both. Removing a key blocks new assertions; issued access tokens' fate after key deletion is not documented.

steps: Regenerate/remove the Primary or Secondary App Token in Developer Console > Configuration; admin disables the app in Admin Console.
notes: Box docs do not document revoking App Tokens or the effect of regeneration; verify in a test app.

steps: Revoke the token in Developer Console or via POST /oauth2/revoke; it also expires on its own after 60 minutes. Disable the developer's account or the app if generation is the problem.
notes: Revoking a developer token deletes all webhooks created by that app.

credential: Personal API tokens (incl. tokens from OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration)
steps: User deletes and recreates the token; remove the user from the org/IdP; block new work and rotate secrets the user could reach.
notes: No admin-side revoke documented.

steps: Delete under Project Settings > API Permissions.
Tighten trust policy; tokens expire within 1 hour.
notes: Cloud session credentials last per provider settings.

credential: Contexts and project environment variables (stored secrets)
steps: Block new work, rotate the secret at its source, update the variable, add context restrictions.
notes: Leaked values stay valid until rotated at the issuing system.

credential: Checkout keys (deploy keys and user keys) and additional SSH keys
steps: Delete key in CircleCI and the public key at GitHub/Bitbucket/GitLab.
notes: Key works at the VCS until its public key is removed there.

steps: Delete or roll the token (DELETE /user/tokens/{token_id}); remove the user from the account if needed.
notes: Roll invalidates the previous token; propagation time not stated.

steps: DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/tokens/{token_id} or roll.
notes: Token survives member removal; must be deleted.

steps: Change the Global API Key in My Profile > API Tokens.
Click Change on the Origin CA key; move integrations to an API token with SSL and Certificates Edit.
notes: Change immediately invalidates all prior values.

steps: Delete the service token (DELETE .../access/service_tokens/{id}); disabling also stops the old secret during a rotation grace period.
notes: Revoking Access sessions alone is not enough.

credential: R2 S3 API credentials (Access Key ID / Secret Access Key)
steps: Delete or roll the parent API token.
notes: Derived temporary credentials stop immediately.

credential: OAuth2/OpenID Connect Client - Client Credentials grant
steps: Deactivate the client in Setup > Integrations > Oauth2/OpenID Connect Clients; add IP Whitelisting.
notes: Tokens are 24h JWTs.

credential: OAuth2/OpenID Connect Client - Authorization Code / Device Code grant (user-delegated)
steps: Deactivate the client.
Edit the key under Setup > Integrations > API Keys and use Revoke API Key.
notes: Static key; revocation removes its API access.

credential: OAuth2 API client (client ID and secret)
steps: Delete the API client or reset its secret; revoke known tokens with POST /oauth2/revoke.
notes: Tokens last up to 30 min if not revoked.

credential: Flight Control (MSSP) parent API client acting on a child CID (member_cid)
steps: Delete or reset the parent API client.

credential: Next-Gen SIEM HEC data connector API key (ingest token)
steps: Regenerate the ingest token or delete the connector.
notes: Regenerating the ingest token invalidates the previous one; timing not stated.

steps: Delete the secret (DELETE /api/2.0/accounts/{account_id}/servicePrincipals/{service_principal}/credentials/secrets/{secret_id}); to stop tokens already minted, deactivate the service principal via the Account Service Principals API, then rotate.
notes: Docs do not say whether deleting a secret invalidates issued access tokens (1-hour lifetime). SP deactivation blocks all its tokens.

steps: Delete or tighten the federation policy (deleteFederationPolicy); deactivate the mapped service principal or user; revoke/rotate trust at the external IdP.
notes: Docs do not state whether deleting a policy invalidates already-exchanged Databricks tokens; those expire at the JWT exp (commonly one hour). SP deactivation blocks its tokens.

steps: Revoke: databricks token-management delete TOKEN_ID (DELETE /api/2.0/token-management/tokens/{token_id}) or account console token report > Revoke; owner can run databricks tokens revoke --token-id. Deactivate owner if compromised.
notes: PAT is the bearer credential itself; docs do not state propagation delay. Tokens of deactivated users are not auto-revoked.

steps: Deactivate the user (account level); delete or disable the OAuth app integration; shorten refresh_token_ttl_in_minutes / enable single-use refresh tokens and absolute_session_lifetime_in_minutes; delete local token-cache.json.
notes: Revoking consent doesn't invalidate existing tokens; refresh tokens work until expiry. No documented per-token revoke for OAuth tokens. Access tokens last one hour.

steps: Revoke API key in Organization Settings > API keys (restorable 7 days); revoke app key in Application Keys (permanent). Rotate: create new key, update services, then revoke.
notes: Revocation may take a few seconds to propagate. Disabling a user revokes their app keys but NOT API keys they created.

steps: Revoke tokens via POST /oauth2/v1/revoke or user revokes app authorization; delete the OAuth client.
notes: Refresh tokens never expire until revoked; access tokens last 1 hour. Not documented whether revoking a refresh token kills issued access tokens.

steps: Delete intake mapping (DELETE /api/v2/cloud_auth/aws/intake_mapping/<MAPPING_UUID>); remove persona mapping; disable mapped service account; revoke the AWS role session on the AWS side.
notes: JWT lifetime not documented; Agent may fall back to configured static API key.

steps: Delete the token in Organization Settings > Client Tokens and ship a new token in the SDK config.
notes: Deletion is permanent; deactivating the creator does not disable it. Token is public by design, so treat as abuse/injection risk, not secret leak.

steps: Revoke the token in the UI or with DELETE on its endpoint; also list and revoke any tokens it created. For PATs, disabling the owner revokes all their PATs.
notes: Docs: revoked tokens can no longer authenticate; takes effect within seconds (eventual consistency).

steps: Revoke the token in the UI or with DELETE on its endpoint; also list and revoke any tokens it created. For PATs, disabling the owner revokes all their PATs.
notes: Docs: revoked tokens can no longer authenticate; takes effect within seconds (eventual consistency).

steps: Revoke the key (API or Settings > Devin API > Service users); or delete the service user.
Admin revokes from PAT inventory, or switch PAT policy to Disabled, or remove the user (auto-revokes).
notes: Rotation stops the old secret immediately; revoke is documented as invalidating the token.

credential: Legacy API keys (Personal apk_user_ / Service apk_)
steps: DELETE /v2/enterprise/api-keys/{api_key_id} or revoke in Settings > API Keys.

User: Manage Profile > Connected Apps > Revoke. Org-granted consent: revoke in Docusign Admin. If client secret leaked: revoke secrets on the integration key (Apps and Keys) and, if needed, ask Docusign to disable the key.
notes: Revoking consent invalidates refresh tokens and blocks new tokens, but live access tokens keep working until they expire (8 h default for auth code).

steps: Revoke consent (user Connected Apps, or Docusign Admin for org consent), then remove/rotate the RSA keypair on the integration key so no new JWT can be signed; deactivate impersonated system user if needed.
notes: Issued JWT-grant access tokens stay valid until expiry (1 hour). Removing the RSA keypair step is from general practice; exact UI step not verified in fetched docs.

steps: Admin: POST team/linked_apps/revoke_linked_app (app_id + team_member_id) or revoke_linked_app_batch; app owner: auth/token/revoke with the token; user: unlink in account settings. Rotate the app secret if the app key/secret leaked. Blocking the app in App permissions does not disconnect existing users.
notes: Docs do not say whether unlinking immediately invalidates issued short-lived access tokens; token/revoke disables only the token used for the call.

steps: Revoke in Organization > API keys or DELETE /api/v1/users/auth/keys/{api_key_id}; bulk via DELETE /api/v1/users/auth/keys.
notes: Also rotate any 'elastic' passwords or ES keys the Cloud key could have created.

credential: Elasticsearch API key (personal/user API key, incl. Serverless project API keys)
steps: DELETE /_security/api_key with ids, or by username/realm_name to kill all of a user's keys.
notes: Invalidated keys fail authentication.

steps: Invalidate via DELETE /_security/api_key on the remote cluster.
Delete the token via API; file-backed tokens need the service_tokens file edited.
notes: Index-backed token cache clears automatically when the security index changes (for example, a token delete); file-backed cache clears on file change. No derived tokens.

steps: Disable the SA (cuts all tokens), then delete the key; rotate dependents.
notes: Key deletion alone leaves minted tokens valid (up to 1h, or 12h if extended).

credential: Short-lived service account credentials (service account impersonation)
steps: Remove Token Creator bindings; disable the SA to kill live tokens.
notes: Disabling the SA is the documented kill for short-lived credentials.

steps: Disable the provider or pool; tighten attribute condition; disable impersonated SA to kill live tokens.
notes: Disabling the pool blocks existing tokens (until re-enabled); disabling a provider only stops new exchanges and existing tokens keep working. Tokens from impersonated service accounts need separate action.

credential: API keys (standard keys and authorization keys bound to a service account)
steps: Delete the key (or add restrictions); for authorization keys also disable the bound SA.
notes: Propagation time for deletion not documented.

steps: Set the key INACTIVE, then delete it.
notes: Deleted HMAC keys are immediately invalid.

steps: Owner deletes token in settings; anyone with the value can POST it to the credential revocation API; org/enterprise owners revoke its SSO authorization or restrict classic PAT access by policy; EMU owners can delete credentials.
notes: Deleting/revoking ends the token. SSO revoke only blocks SSO-protected orgs; token still works elsewhere. Org owners cannot list classic PATs.

steps: Owner deletes token; anyone posts value to revocation API; org owner revokes it (UI or REST via GitHub App); restrict PAT access by org/enterprise policy.
notes: Org-owner revoke leaves SSH keys created by the token working and public reads allowed; user can reassign resource owner. Full delete or API revocation kills it.

steps: App owner calls DELETE /installation/token; org owner suspends or uninstalls the app; rotate the app private key so no new tokens can be minted.
notes: Uninstall deactivates all installation tokens; tokens expire in 1 hour anyway. Not covered by enterprise bulk SSO/credential actions. Private-key rotation event name not established.

steps: User revokes app authorization; app owner DELETE /applications/{client_id}/token or /grant; anyone posts ghu_/ghr_ to revocation API; org owner suspends/uninstalls the app; integration.revoke_all_tokens.
notes: Revoking authorization revokes all its tokens across all orgs. Org owners cannot revoke user authorizations or their SSO authorization directly.

steps: Cancel in-progress runs; disable Actions for repo/org; remove self-hosted runners; set default workflow permissions to read.
notes: No manual revocation; token dies at job end. Not affected by enterprise bulk credential actions. Rotate any other secrets exposed to the job.

steps: User revokes authorization; app owner DELETE /applications/{client_id}/token or /grant or revoke all tokens; anyone posts value to revocation API; org owner denies the app's org access; reset client secret.
notes: Revoking authorization kills all its tokens. Org owners cannot revoke an OAuth token's SSO authorization; denying app access blocks org data.

steps: Repo admin deletes the key (UI or DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys/{key_id}); org owner disables deploy keys org-wide; enterprise policy can disable them.
notes: Org-wide disable disables existing keys immediately. Not covered by enterprise bulk credential actions or SSO revoke.

steps: DELETE /personal_access_tokens/:id (or self); DELETE /projects/:id/access_tokens/:token_id or groups equivalent; or revoke in UI. Admins can revoke any user's PAT; Self-Managed admins can identify a leaked value via POST /admin/token.
notes: Revocation is immediate. Rotation revokes the old token at once. Rotating a revoked token revokes the whole token family. Blocking/deleting an enterprise user auto-revokes their PATs.

steps: User revokes the app under Access > Applications > Authorized applications; app owner calls POST /oauth/revoke with client_id, client_secret, token; delete the application to remove all grants and tokens; Renew secret to stop the app from obtaining new tokens.
notes: Deleting the app removes all tokens. Effect of revoking a refresh token on outstanding access tokens is not documented; access tokens expire after 2 hours.

steps: Cancel the running job; tighten inbound allowlist (remove projects/groups, re-enable inbound scope); restrict fine-grained job token permissions; block the triggering user if their access is abused.
notes: Token is invalid once the job is no longer running. Allowlist changes limit cross-project reach.

steps: DELETE /personal_access_tokens/:id or revoke in UI; admins can revoke any user's token.
notes: Revocation is immediate; rotation revokes the previous token.

steps: Revoke the token in Admin console > Platform > API tokens.
Revoke the global token in the API tokens page.
Revoke the token in API tokens (Indexing tab).
notes: After a rotation the old secret works for 10 more minutes.

credential: Glean OAuth Authorization Server token (static and DCR clients, MCP)
steps: Delete/revoke the client; sign the user out of all sessions.
notes: Takes effect after ~5-10 min propagation / 10 min cache. Users can also revoke an app themselves, which deletes its consents and refresh tokens. Admins can list a static client's users via View users.

steps: Revoke in IdP; remove client ID or disable IdP OAuth in Glean.
notes: Revocation follows the IdP's policies. Docs do not say whether Glean checks revocation for each request or accepts tokens until they expire.

credential: Enterprise Managed Auth (JWT bearer assertion for MCP)
steps: Turn off EMA or remove the trusted issuer; unassign the user in the IdP.
notes: Turning off EMA or removing the issuer leaves existing tokens valid until expiry. Admin 'sign out of all sessions' invalidates them after the revocation cache refreshes (~10 minutes).

steps: Admin: Directory API tokens.delete for user+clientId; add the app to the blocked list (ADD_TO_BLOCKED_OAUTH2_APPS); user/app: POST token to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke; reset user if account compromised.
notes: Revoking an access token also revokes its refresh token; tokens.delete removes all access tokens for that user+app.

steps: Delete or disable the key; remove the client ID from domain-wide delegation; disable the service account to stop issued short-lived credentials; review and remove IAM bindings.
notes: Disabling a key does not revoke short-lived credentials already issued from it; disabling or deleting the service account does.

steps: Private app > Auth > Rotate > 'Rotate and expire now'; or delete the private app (token permanently revoked). Then update the integration with the new token.
notes: 'Rotate and expire later' leaves the old token valid for 7 days; use expire now for incidents.

steps: Uninstall the app from Settings > Integrations > Connected apps; app owner deletes refresh token (DELETE /oauth/v1/refresh-tokens/{token}); rotate client secret if it leaked.
notes: Deleting a refresh token does not delete access tokens already issued; those last up to 30 minutes. Effect of uninstall on live access tokens not documented.

steps: Super admin or developer seat: rotate the token on the app's Distribution tab; or uninstall the app from the account.
notes: Fetched docs do not describe expire-now vs expire-later semantics for static tokens.

steps: Development > Keys > Developer API key: deactivate the key and generate a new one.
notes: Docs say the key can be deactivated at any time; timing of enforcement not stated.

steps: Development > Keys > Service keys > key > Rotate > 'Rotate and expire now'; or Delete the key.
notes: 'Rotate and expire later' keeps the old key valid for 7 days.

steps: Enterprise: revoke org access via API; for full kill submit the token to POST /api/credentials/revoke or have owner delete it.
notes: Org revoke stops org access; credentials/revoke invalidates everywhere immediately.

steps: Enable fine-grained-only policy, revoke org access (Enterprise), or global revoke via POST /api/credentials/revoke.
Rotate or delete the token in Service Accounts settings.
notes: Old value stops working immediately on rotate.

credential: OAuth app access token (Sign in with HF)
steps: User revokes the app in their settings (path not documented).
Refresh the OAuth app client secret; issued tokens expire per configured duration.
notes: Effect of secret refresh on issued tokens not stated.

steps: Remove the trusted publisher from repo settings (or CI/CD identity from account).
notes: Tokens expire within 60 minutes.

credential: Jamf Pro API client (API Roles and Clients, client credentials)
steps: Disable or delete the client and rotate its secret; to cut live tokens immediately, remove privileges from the client's API roles (role changes apply to live tokens).
notes: Disable/delete leaves valid tokens working until expiry; role edits apply immediately.

credential: Jamf Pro user account bearer token (username/password via /v1/auth/token)
steps: Disable/delete the user account or change its password; holder can call POST /v1/auth/invalidate-token.
notes: Docs do not say whether disabling an account invalidates outstanding bearer tokens.

credential: Jamf Platform API Gateway integration (Jamf Account client credentials)
steps: Delete or regenerate the integration in Jamf Account.
notes: Jamf's migration guide lists no invalidate endpoint for gateway tokens; they expire after 900 s.

credential: Jamf Protect API client (client ID + API client password)
steps: Delete the API client in Administrative > API Clients.
Remove the key under Organization > Settings > API.
notes: Delete is not explicitly documented.

credential: Access tokens (scoped tokens: admin, user, group and project scopes; reference token form)
steps: Revoke by ID or by value; disable the user; for refreshable tokens without SCIM, disable the JFrog user directly.
notes: Tokens below the revocable threshold (default 6h) cannot be revoked and run to expiry.

steps: Revoke in profile/admin UI or disable the user.
notes: User disable revokes tokens.

steps: Enable Disable API Key Usage; revoke the user's key.
notes: Checkbox blocks API key usage platform-wide.

steps: Delete or tighten the identity mapping / OIDC configuration.
notes: Tokens with expiry below revocable-expiry-threshold (default 6 hours) cannot be revoked and run until expiry; longer ones can be revoked.

steps: Regenerate the token.
notes: Old token expires on regeneration.

steps: Deactivate or delete in Settings > API Keys (All members) or via revocation API; remove user from org.
notes: Takes effect within about a minute due to auth cache.

steps: Delete the key (Settings > API Keys > Service, or DELETE /api/v1/orgs/current/service-keys/{api_key_id}).
notes: Auth cache means up to about a minute.

steps: DELETE /v1/platform/orgs/current/scim/tokens/{scim_token_id}
POST /key/block or /key/delete; for master key, change LITELLM_MASTER_KEY and restart all instances.
notes: Restart loads the new value; old value no longer matches.

steps: POST /key/block or /key/delete; for master key, change LITELLM_MASTER_KEY and restart all instances.
notes: Block/delete is immediate on the worker that handles it. Without Redis, other workers keep accepting the key until their cache entry expires (user_api_key_cache_ttl, default 60 s). SCIM deprovisioning is documented as immediate.

steps: POST /key/block or /key/delete; for master key, change LITELLM_MASTER_KEY and restart all instances.
notes: Same per-worker cache behaviour as virtual keys: without Redis, a revoked key works on other workers until user_api_key_cache_ttl (default 60 s) expires.

credential: OIDC / JWT-based auth (incl. Kubernetes ServiceAccount tokens)
steps: Revoke at the IdP, remove the issuer/JWKS URL from config, or rotate signing keys.
notes: Issued JWTs remain valid until exp unless the issuer is removed; JWKS cached for public_key_ttl.

steps: Not documented; manage in Settings > Admin Settings > SCIM.
Call revokeSignInSessions for the user; remove the delegated permission grant / user consent; disable the service principal or block the app if malicious; reset password if user is compromised.
notes: Refresh tokens die (few-minute delay). Issued access tokens live 60-90 min unless client and resource support CAE, which revokes in near real time.

steps: Remove the compromised secret/cert (app registration or service principal); remove app role assignments; disable the service principal (accountEnabled false) or delete it.
notes: Removing a credential stops new tokens; already-issued app-only access tokens stay valid until expiry (default 60-90 min).

steps: Remove role/app-role assignments; delete federated credentials; detach identity from the resource or delete it; for user-assigned MIs use the revokeTokens action; stop or isolate the host resource.
notes: MI tokens are cached ~24h per resource URI and cannot be force-refreshed, so permission removal can take hours. revokeTokens exists only for user-assigned identities.

credential: Service account (Atlas Administration API, OAuth 2.0 client credentials)
steps: Revoke tokens via POST /api/oauth/revoke, delete the secret or the service account, remove access list entries.
notes: Docs do not say whether deleting the secret invalidates issued tokens; revoke tokens explicitly. Tokens last at most 1 hour.

steps: Delete the API key (UI, atlas organizations apiKeys delete, or Admin API).
notes: Digest auth checks the key on each request, so deletion should stop further calls; not explicitly stated.

steps: Delete the user or change its password; tighten project IP access list.
notes: Docs say clients lose access once the user is deleted; open sessions not addressed.

steps: Delete the database user.
notes: Individual certificates cannot be revoked.

steps: Delete the Atlas database user or revoke the IAM role sessions in AWS.
Delete the mapped database user/group or disable the identity provider.
notes: Disconnecting the IdP removes Workload Identity Federation access; Revoke JWKS immediately drops cached keys but clients must be restarted. Docs do not say open connections are closed.

credential: Connected app that acts on its own behalf (client credentials)
steps: Rotate the secret (Modify the Client Secret) or delete the app in Access Management > Connected Apps; remove scopes.
notes: DELETE /accounts/api/organizations/{organizationId}/connectedApplications/{clientId}/revoke revokes all access and refresh tokens issued to the app. Rotating the secret alone is not documented to kill issued tokens.

credential: Connected app that acts on behalf of a user (authorization code, refresh token, password, JWT bearer)
steps: Access Management > Connected Apps > Authorizations > Remove; also rotate secret.
notes: Docs: access and refresh tokens are revoked; cannot be undone.

credential: Anypoint Platform bearer token (user token from /accounts/login or SAML assertion)
steps: Disable/remove the user or wait for session timeout.
notes: The user can end their own session with GET /accounts/logout; no admin-side per-token revoke is documented. Otherwise the token lasts until the Default Session Timeout.

credential: Environment / business group client ID and client secret
steps: Reset environment client_secret per KB or contact support.

credential: API client application credentials (client ID / secret for API instances)
steps: Revoke the contract in API Manager, then reset secret or delete the app.
notes: Revoke blocks the client app from the API.

steps: Delete the key in Settings > n8n API (as the key owner). On self-hosted, N8N_PUBLIC_API_DISABLED=true stops all key use.
notes: Docs do not say whether deletion is immediate.

credential: MCP access token (instance-level MCP, API key tab)
steps: Owner rotates the token (revokes old). Admin can disable instance MCP, which revokes all clients.
notes: Rotation revokes the previous token; no token creation event documented.

steps: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > Revoke access (all-users view for others).
notes: Client is disconnected at once.

credential: Token exchange access token (OEM embedding, preview)
steps: Remove the trusted key entry; set N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_ENABLED=false.
notes: Issued tokens stay valid until expiry (default max 15 min).

credential: Stored credentials (third-party secrets held by n8n)
steps: Rotate the secret at the external service, then update or delete the n8n credential.
Settings → Connections → Develop or manage connections → Refresh the internal connection token (or delete the connection); remove page access; update apps with new token.
notes: Docs say to replace the old token everywhere after Refresh but do not state explicitly that the old token is invalidated immediately. Deleting the connection removes it.

steps: Creator revokes in Developer portal, or admin revokes in Settings → Connections → All personal access tokens, or Admin API DELETE /v1/spaces/{space_id}/personal_access_tokens/{bot_id}. Optionally tighten PAT creation policy.
notes: Revocation is immediate and permanent; token stops working for API and Workers.

steps: App operator: POST /v1/oauth/revoke with the token (Basic auth with client id/secret). Workspace owner: Settings → Connections → disconnect the connection or disconnect members. Remove from approved connections.
notes: Revoke endpoint revokes the given access token; docs do not say if sibling refresh/access tokens or other authorizations are revoked. Since 2026-06-08 each authorization mints a fresh pair, so one user may hold several.

steps: Organization console → Manage organization-level admin API tokens → delete/revoke the token; review audit log for actions with that admin bot as actor.
notes: Help doc: any script using the token stops immediately. Admin tokens cannot be IP-restricted.

steps: Revoke by ID: Security > API > Tokens, or DELETE /api/v1/api-tokens/{apiTokenId}. Deactivating the owning user deprovisions all their tokens. Add a network condition (PUT /api/v1/api-tokens/{apiTokenId}) to restrict use while investigating.
notes: SSWS tokens are validated per request, so revocation stops use. Unused tokens expire after 30 days. Review what the token created (other tokens, OAuth apps, admin roles).

steps: Deactivate the attacker's JWK/secret (POST /api/v1/apps/{appId}/credentials/jwks/{keyId}/lifecycle/deactivate or .../secrets/{secretId}/lifecycle/deactivate) or deactivate the app (/api/v1/apps/{appId}/lifecycle/deactivate). Remove granted okta.* scopes and admin roles.
notes: Revoking keys stops new tokens. 'Revoke all application tokens' only covers refresh-token-derived access tokens; client-credentials access tokens are not affected and live up to 1 hour. Effect of app deactivation on issued tokens not documented.

steps: Developer > Service accounts > account > Revoke Token, or delete the service account; or turn off Service Account Access on affected vaults.
notes: Docs: revoke immediately removes access; deleted SA token can't authenticate.

steps: Developer > Connect servers > environment > gear > Revoke; or remove vault access from the environment.
notes: Immediate effect not stated.

credential: SCIM bridge / automated provisioning bearer token
steps: Integrations > Automated User Provisioning > Regenerate Credentials, or turn off Provisioning users & groups.
notes: Old token invalidation not explicitly stated.

steps: Integrations > Events Reporting integration > gear > Revoke.
notes: Docs say SIEM stops ingesting after revoke.

steps: Integrations > OAuth Application > Revoke integration (kills all tokens), or POST /v1/oauth/revoke per token.
notes: Revoke integration revokes all access tokens.

steps: Delete the key in the dashboard or DELETE /v1/organization/projects/{project_id}/api_keys/{api_key_id}.
notes: Revocations take effect within a few seconds.

steps: Delete the key, or delete the service account.
notes: Key revocation takes effect within a few seconds; service account deletion effect on live keys assumed but not stated.

steps: Delete via dashboard admin-keys page or DELETE /v1/organization/admin_api_keys/{key_id}.
notes: Docs state API key revocation takes effect within a few seconds; the statement is for API keys in general, not admin keys specifically. Keys are per-request bearer secrets with no derived tokens.

steps: Disable or delete the service account mapping or provider; delete the service account.
notes: Tokens expire within an hour; immediate invalidation of issued tokens not stated.

steps: Delete the key from the API keys page.
notes: General API key statement: revocations take effect within a few seconds; legacy keys not named specifically.

credential: Confidential service client (organization, extension app, tenant-level or app-level) - client credentials
steps: Admin Center > Service clients > Revoke client, then Regenerate client; or PATCH the client with activate=false.
notes: Docs say Revoke client revokes an access token but do not state scope or timing.

credential: Resource owner password grant (confidential client + user name/password)
steps: Revoke the confidential client; reset the user's password.
notes: Docs say Revoke client revokes an access token but do not state scope or timing.

credential: User access/refresh tokens via authorization code (confidential) or PKCE (public client)
steps: Revoke the confidential client; for public clients deactivate via Admin API activate=false; disable the user.
notes: Docs say Revoke client revokes an access token but do not state scope or timing.

credential: General Access REST API Key (account API key)
steps: Integrations > Developer Tools > API Access Keys: Disable (reversible) or Remove (permanent). Issue a replacement key first if SCIM or recovery depends on it.
notes: Docs say a disabled key stops working with the REST API; timing not stated. Keep one key for IP-allow-list lockout recovery.

credential: User Token REST API Key (personal REST API key)
steps: User or Admin: User Settings > API Access > Remove. Removing the user from the account disables their keys.
notes: Admins cannot remove keys of Admins/Global Admins/Account Owner; those users must remove their own.

credential: Scoped OAuth app token (private app, client credentials)
steps: App Registration > app > OAuth Client > Revoke All Tokens, then delete and recreate OAuth functionality to replace the client secret (revoke first: deleting does not revoke tokens).
notes: Docs say Revoke All Tokens invalidates all tokens; app tokens otherwise expire in 1 day.

credential: User OAuth token (Scoped OAuth and Classic User OAuth apps)
steps: Integrations > OAuth Apps > app > Revoke All User Tokens or Uninstall; per-user: DELETE /oauth_delegations or admin password change.
notes: Revoke All runs in the background; delegation deletion is synchronous.

steps: Services > service > Integrations > Edit Integration > Generate a new integration key, or Delete Integration.
notes: Rotation overwrites the key immediately; old key presumably rejected (not stated).

steps: Generate a new secret and revoke the previous secret, remove role assignments, or disable/delete the app. Existing access tokens cannot be revoked; removing roles cuts access on the next call.
notes: Role removal is checked per call (S5); token revocation is not available for PingOne API tokens (S8).

steps: Remove the user's admin roles, disable the app, or delete the user. Revoke refresh tokens at /as/revoke only applies to custom-resource tokens.
notes: PingOne API access tokens cannot be revoked; roles are checked per call.

steps: DELETE /v1/environments/{envID}/gateways/{gatewayID}/credentials/{credentialID}
notes: Docs say all instances using it lose their credentials; already-exchanged access tokens not addressed.

steps: DELETE the key via Admin API or dashboard; or rotate with minimum 30-minute transition.
notes: Rotation leaves old secret valid at least 30 minutes.

steps: DELETE the key via Admin API or dashboard; or rotate with minimum 30-minute transition.
notes: Rotation leaves old secret valid at least 30 minutes.

steps: DELETE the key via Admin API or dashboard; or rotate with minimum 30-minute transition.
notes: Rotation leaves old secret valid at least 30 minutes.

steps: Remove or rotate the JWKS entry; revoke at issuer.
notes: Valid JWTs work until exp unless JWKS removed.

steps: Regenerate in Admin Settings > Authentication Settings > SCIM Provisioning (revocation of old token not documented).
Rotate the key at the upstream provider and update/delete the integration.
notes: Upstream rotation ends use.

steps: Revoke in Organization > Postman Keys (or Revoke all); owner can delete in Account settings > API keys.
notes: Docs do not state propagation time; key is checked per request via header.

credential: System service account API key and access token
steps: Service Accounts > select account > revoke or delete key.
notes: Issued short-lived tokens may remain valid until expiry; not documented.

steps: Turn off, regenerate or delete the key under Service Accounts or Organization settings > Authentication.
notes: Regeneration may keep old key active if chosen.

steps: Delete key in API keys page or Manage public elements, or DELETE /collection-access-keys/{keyId}.
notes: Revocation is permanent.

steps: POST /oauth2/token/revoke with the token.
notes: Docs: revocation is immediate.

steps: Delete the PAT (owner UI or DELETE /personal-access-tokens/{id}).
notes: Docs say scope changes don't affect existing bearer tokens; deletion effect on live bearer tokens (default 12h) not documented.

steps: Delete via API Management Bulk Delete or DELETE /oauth-clients/{id}; or PATCH enabled=false.
notes: Not documented whether issued access tokens die at once.

credential: API client - authorization code / refresh token
steps: Delete or disable the API client.
notes: Refresh token revocation endpoint not documented.

steps: Delete the VA, then shut down the VA instance.
notes: Rotation of keyPassphrase not covered here.

steps: POST refresh token (or OauthToken DeleteToken) to /services/oauth2/revoke; revoke the app's tokens for the user in Setup; delete AuthSession rows; block or edit the connected app / rotate consumer secret; freeze user.
notes: Revoking a refresh token also revokes its associated access tokens.

steps: Remove or replace the certificate on the connected app; remove pre-authorized profiles/permission sets; revoke current access tokens via /services/oauth2/revoke; delete AuthSession rows; freeze the integration user.
notes: No refresh token exists, so attacker re-mints with the private key until the cert or pre-authorization is removed. Issued access tokens need explicit revoke or session deletion.

steps: Disable or fix the SAML/IdP configuration or rotate its certificate; revoke tokens via /services/oauth2/revoke; delete AuthSession rows; freeze affected users.
notes: Issued tokens remain until revoked or sessions deleted.

steps: Set handler IsEnabled to false; revoke issued tokens via /services/oauth2/revoke; delete AuthSession rows; fix handler Apex validation; revoke the upstream IdP token.
notes: Disabling the handler stops new exchanges only.

credential: XSUAA service key / service binding (OAuth client credentials: binding-secret or X.509)
steps: Delete the binding or service key (cf unbind-service / delete-service-key); create a replacement first. Shorten token-validity; for apps validating offline, wait for expiry or rotate signing keys.
notes: Secret stops working at once, but already-issued JWTs remain valid in offline-validating apps until expiry.

steps: btp delete security/api-credential
notes: Issued tokens follow XSUAA token validity.

credential: SAP Cloud Management service (cis) service key
steps: Delete the cis service key (and instance if needed); reset the user's password for password-grant keys.
notes: Issued tokens live until expiry.

steps: Remove the user's role collections or disable the user at the IdP; token expires within 12h.
notes: No server-side session revocation documented.

credential: SAP Cloud Identity Services client ID/secret or certificate (applications, systems as administrators, technical users)
steps: Delete the secret/certificate, the system administrator, or the technical user in the admin console.
notes: Effect on already-issued tokens not documented.

credential: S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition communication user (basic auth or X.509) in a communication arrangement
steps: Lock or delete the user in Maintain Communication Users; change its password; remove its certificate.
notes: Security sessions created with x-sap-security-session may persist; effect of lock on them not documented.

steps: Revoke Access on the token record in Manage Tokens, or call oauth_revoke_token.do with the token; deactivate the OAuth application registry entry; lock the user.
notes: oauth_revoke_token.do or Manage Tokens > Revoke Access marks the given token expired. Docs do not say that revoking a refresh token also expires access tokens already issued from it (default 30-minute life).

steps: Disable the OIDC provider / third-party ID token integration; revoke issued tokens in Manage Tokens or via oauth_revoke_token.do; revoke the upstream IdP session.
notes: Upstream ID token revocation does not reach tokens ServiceNow already issued.

steps: Set the REST API Key Active to false or delete it; lock or deactivate the key's user; tighten REST API access policy.
notes: Each request presents the key, so deactivation should stop use; not confirmed in docs.

steps: Reset the password; lock or deactivate the user; restrict account to web service access or move it to OAuth/API key with access policy.
notes: Existing sessions may persist; session termination not covered in fetched docs.

steps: Set the REST API HMAC Secret Active to false or delete it; rotate the shared secret; lock the user.
notes: Per-request signing implies immediate effect; not confirmed in docs.

steps: Call auth.revoke with the leaked token; or uninstall the app (apps.uninstall, or admin.apps.uninstall with app_id + enterprise_id/team_ids); restrict the app to block reinstall; rotate the client secret before reinstall.
notes: auth.revoke kills one token only; other user/bot tokens of the same app stay valid until uninstall. Revoking a bot token deactivates the bot user and removes its channel memberships but does not uninstall the app.

steps: auth.revoke the access token(s); uninstall the app (apps.uninstall / admin.apps.uninstall) to kill the refresh chain; rotate client_secret since it is required for refresh; reinstall.
notes: Refreshing does not immediately invalidate the old access token; old refresh token is revoked after a short grace period. auth.revoke revokes a single token without changing the installation. Up to 2 active access tokens can exist at once.

steps: Remove the user's or app's access in the IdP (Okta) so no new ID-JAG is issued; uninstall or restrict the MCP client app in Slack; auth.revoke any captured xoxp token.
notes: auth.revoke kills one access token at once, but the client's long-lived IdP credential can mint new tokens until the IdP or app side is revoked. EMA docs do not describe revocation.

steps: Owner deletes the token under Personal Settings > API Access, or call DELETE /token with it. Admin: deactivate the user (revokes all their tokens), then reissue as needed.
notes: Revoked token fails on later calls. Admin revocation of a single token of another user is not documented.

credential: OAuth 2.0 app (authorization code; access + refresh tokens)
steps: Call DELETE /token?deleteAllForApiClient=true with a token for that app and user; or set a short plan-wide expiration.
notes: Requires holding a token for the app. Whether user deactivation or a UI action revokes OAuth grants is not documented.

steps: Identify owner of a found secret with SELECT SYSTEM$DECODE_PAT('<secret>'); run ALTER USER <u> REMOVE PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN <name> (or MODIFY … SET DISABLED = TRUE to preserve for review). For wider compromise, ALTER USER <u> SET DISABLED = TRUE, which aborts running queries and disables the user's PATs.
notes: Docs do not say whether sessions opened with a PAT end on removal. ALTER USER SET DISABLED = TRUE aborts running queries. Removed PATs drop out of CREDENTIALS, so snapshot the row before removing.

steps: ALTER USER <u> REMOVE DELEGATED AUTHORIZATIONS FROM SECURITY INTEGRATION <int> (per user), or REMOVE DELEGATED AUTHORIZATIONS OF ANY ROLE FROM SECURITY INTEGRATION <int>; disable the integration (ENABLED = FALSE) for client-wide compromise; ALTER USER SET DISABLED = TRUE for user compromise.
notes: ALTER USER docs say removal revokes OAuth access tokens for the integration, and SESSIONS has CLOSED_REASON OAUTH_CONSENT_REVOKED; whether all open sessions close is not stated.

steps: ALTER USER <u> REMOVE KEY PAIR <name> or UNSET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY / RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2; or ROTATE KEY PAIR with EXPIRE_ROTATED_KEY_PAIR_AFTER_HOURS = 0; ALTER USER <u> SET DISABLED = TRUE to abort running queries.
notes: Each JWT is valid at most 1 hour; docs do not say whether sessions opened with a removed key end.

steps: ALTER USER <u> REMOVE WORKLOAD IDENTITY <name> or MODIFY … to disable; UNSET WORKLOAD_IDENTITY for DEFAULT; ALTER USER <u> SET DISABLED = TRUE; also revoke the cloud role/federated credential on the provider side.
notes: Snowflake caches issuer signing keys up to 60 minutes; session behavior after removal is not documented.

steps: Revoke tokens/sessions and disable the user at the IdP; ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION <int> SET ENABLED = FALSE for issuer compromise; ALTER USER <u> SET DISABLED = TRUE to abort running queries and block login.
notes: Snowflake validates IdP tokens locally; docs do not describe revoking an IdP-issued token in Snowflake, so issued tokens may stay usable until expiry unless the user or integration is disabled.

steps: Owner revokes in Account settings > Personal access tokens or DELETE /rest/self/personal_access_tokens/{id}. Admins can only remove the user from Group/Orgs.
notes: Docs say revocation cannot be reverted but do not say whether in-flight access ends instantly.

credential: Snyk API token (legacy personal API token)
steps: Owner clicks Revoke & Regenerate at app.snyk.io/account.
notes: Integrations using the key stop immediately.

credential: Service account token (auth_type access_token or legacy api_key)
steps: Delete the service account in Settings > Service accounts or DELETE /rest/{groups|orgs}/{id}/service_accounts/{serviceaccount_id}.
notes: Token invalidated immediately.

steps: Replace secret (POST .../secrets mode replace) or delete the service account.
notes: Deleting revokes credentials; whether already-issued access tokens (up to TTL) stop working on secret replace is not stated.

credential: Snyk Apps (OAuth 2.0 apps: user or tenant context)
steps: Revoke the install (UI or DELETE /rest/groups/{group_id}/apps/installs/{install_id}), revoke refresh token via POST /oauth2/revoke, or delete the app.
notes: Refresh token revoked immediately; whether issued access tokens die before TTL is not stated.

steps: Dashboard > API keys > Rotate key with Expiration 'Now' (deletes old key) or Expire key. Managed keys: rotate in Dashboard or on hosting platform. Then review the key's request logs, and apply an access policy to the replacement key.
notes: Rotation defaults allow old key to keep working up to 7 days; choose 'Now' for compromise. Keys are bearer secrets with no sessions, so expiry stops all further use. Stripe may proactively deactivate detected exposed keys.

credential: Stripe Apps OAuth (Connect OAuth tokens deprecated)
steps: Installing account: uninstall the app (Settings > Installed apps). Developer: rotate the developer secret key used at /v1/oauth/token (stripe-1) and delete stored refresh tokens. Connect OAuth (deprecated) platforms: POST https://connect.stripe.com/oauth/deauthorize.
notes: Docs do not state whether uninstall immediately invalidates issued access/refresh tokens. Access tokens expire after 1 hour regardless.

steps: Organization Dashboard > API keys tab (org/api-keys/secret): rotate or expire the sk_org key; then review org-level Workbench logs per account.
notes: Org-key rotate/expire semantics are not separately documented; assume same as account keys (7-day grace unless expired now).

steps: Cloud side: remove the WIF inline policy / revoke role sessions (AWS) or remove token-creator grants and disable the service account (GCP). Stripe side: edit or delete the service principal / subject in Organization > Developers > API authentication > Service principals.
notes: Exchanged tokens expire in 1 hour; docs do not say whether deleting the service principal revokes tokens already issued.

steps: Delete the token in Principals > Tokens or with sdm admin tokens delete. Prefer delete over rotate: rotation lets existing authentications live up to 24 hours.
notes: Docs say delete is immediate, but the rotate tooltip says existing authentications expire after 24 hours.

steps: Delete the key in Principals > Tokens; there is no rotate, so create a replacement first if automation needs it.
notes: Signed requests are checked per call, so deletion blocks further requests.

steps: Suspend the service account in Users, or rekey it.
notes: Effect on open resource sessions not documented.

steps: Not documented; deactivating SCIM provisioning in Settings > User Management > Provisioning is the likely path.
Delete the node in Networking and create a new one with a new token.
Create secondary token, then promote it to delete the old primary; repeat for affected subaccounts.
notes: Docs say apps using old token stop immediately; Functions may take ~1 minute to pick up change.

steps: Delete the key in Console or DELETE https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Keys/{Sid}.
notes: Also invalidates Access Tokens signed with it.

steps: Rotate secret with grace period 0, or delete the app.
notes: Invalidates previous credentials and access tokens.

credential: Organization OAuth app (Client Credentials / Authorization Code)
steps: Delete the org OAuth app or rotate its secret with grace 0.

credential: Public Key Client Validation (signed request JWT)
steps: Delete the public key credential and the API key used as iss.
notes: Deleting the API key used as iss revokes REST API authentication. Docs do not separately describe deleting the public key credential.

steps: Delete the signing API key.

credential: Integration System User (ISU) user name and password
steps: Change the ISU password and/or restrict it with an authentication policy; exact disable task not public.
notes: Session Timeout 0 means ISU sessions do not time out.

credential: API Client for Integrations with refresh token (Manage Refresh Tokens for Integrations)
steps: Disable the affected OAuth 2.0 client; regenerate the refresh token; review the ISU's security groups.
notes: Workday says compromised access tokens can be replayed within their lifetime.

credential: API Client with JWT Bearer Grant (x509 public key)
steps: Disable the API client and replace the x509 public key.
notes: Access tokens already issued may be replayable until expiry.

steps: Disable the API client; reset the user's sessions/password as needed.
DELETE /api/v2/oauth/tokens/{id} (or POST /api/v2/oauth/tokens/delete_many); for a leaked client secret, PUT /api/v2/oauth/clients/{id}/generate_secret or DELETE the client.
notes: Revoking a token record ends that token. Effect of client deletion on existing tokens not documented. Non-expiring legacy tokens persist until revoked.

steps: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > API tokens: Deactivate (immediate), then Delete. Consider turning off API token access and migrating to OAuth.
notes: Docs: 'As soon as you deactivate a token, API calls using that token begin failing.' Deactivated tokens can be reactivated until deleted.

steps: POST https://zoom.us/oauth/revoke with token=<access_token>; admin Manage > Apps on Account > Added Apps > Disable App or Remove (account-wide) or Disable per user; rotate client secret via POST /marketplace/apps/{appId}/rotate_client_secret with revoke_old_secret_time=now.
notes: Docs do not say whether revoking an access token also kills the refresh token, or whether admin Disable/Remove revokes issued tokens. Access tokens expire after one hour; refresh tokens after 90 days.

steps: Deactivate the app (App Marketplace > app > Activation > Deactivate); rotate the secret via POST /marketplace/apps/{appId}/rotate_client_secret with revoke_old_secret_time=now (dashboard regenerate leaves old secret valid 30 days); delete the app if no longer needed.
notes: Docs: tokens stop working when the app is deactivated. Rotating the secret alone does not kill issued access tokens (1 hour TTL); new tokens do not invalidate old ones. No refresh token.

steps: Disable or delete the API client (revokes its tokens), or revoke individual tokens on the Tokens page; remove secrets/keys.
notes: Revoked tokens can no longer be used; disabling the client revokes its tokens.

credential: OneAPI API client (JWKS URL or certificate/public key)
steps: Disable or delete the API client (revokes its tokens), or revoke individual tokens on the Tokens page; remove secrets/keys.
notes: Revoked tokens can no longer be used; disabling the client revokes its tokens.

credential: Cloud Service API Key with ZIA admin credentials (legacy ZIA API)
steps: Regenerate, edit or delete the Cloud Service API Key; reset or remove the admin account used.
notes: Docs: deleting the key ensures no further API requests are possible; old key invalidated immediately.

credential: ZIA OAuth 2.0 with external authorization server (PingFederate, Okta, Entra ID)
steps: Disable or delete the authorization server in ZIA; disable the client in the IdP; tighten the API role.
notes: Docs do not say whether ZIA rejects already-issued, unexpired JWTs after IdP-side revocation.

credential: ZPA API key (client ID and client secret, legacy ZPA API)
steps: Disable or delete the ZPA API key.
notes: Docs do not say whether issued tokens end before their validity interval (max 3,600 s).

credential: Sandbox API Token with ZIA admin credentials
steps: Regenerate or delete the Sandbox API token.
notes: Regeneration immediately invalidates the old token; effect on open sessions not stated.
